title: In 2 Kings 2 How Can We Apply Elishas Request For A Double Portion Of Elijahs Spirit In Our Own Lives And Ministries
paragraphs: Elisha’s Request for a Double Portion: Understanding Its Meaning and Application

The striking moment in 2 Kings 2 captures Elisha’s bold request of Elijah: a “double portion” of his spirit. This passage is rich with spiritual lessons, offering insight into the nature of godly leadership, spiritual desire, and dependence on God’s power. Let’s examine the context, meaning, and practical application of Elisha’s request for our lives and ministries today.
The Context: A Moment of Transition

As Elijah prepares to be taken up by God, Elisha faithfully follows him from Gilgal to Bethel, Jericho, and finally the Jordan. When Elijah invites Elisha to ask for something before he is taken away, Elisha responds:
And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me. - 2 Kings 2:9 ASV
Elisha’s request is not about personal gain or ambition but reflects a deep spiritual hunger and a desire to be equipped for God’s calling on his life.
What Did the “Double Portion” Mean?

The phrase “double portion” alludes to the inheritance rights of the firstborn son in ancient Israel (Deuteronomy 21:17 ASV). Elisha is essentially asking to be Elijah’s principal spiritual successor—his “firstborn” among the prophets—not necessarily to surpass Elijah’s greatness, but to be fully equipped and empowered to continue his ministry.

Elijah’s response affirms that this is a difficult request, but if Elisha witnesses Elijah’s departure, it will be granted (2 Kings 2:10 ASV). This underscores that the granting of spiritual power and ministry effectiveness is ultimately God’s prerogative.
Application: How Can We Seek a “Double Portion” Today?
Desire for God’s Power, Not Personal Glory
Elisha’s heart was for God’s work, not his own fame. Our ministries should be marked by a longing for God’s Spirit to work through us, rather than for recognition.
But ye shall receive power, when the Holy Spirit is come upon you: and ye shall be my witnesses... - Acts 1:8 ASV
Bold Prayers that Align with God’s Will
Elisha asked boldly, yet his prayer was in line with God’s purpose. We are encouraged to ask God for the spiritual gifts and empowerment needed for our calling.
Let us therefore draw near with boldness unto the throne of grace... - Hebrews 4:16 ASV
Faithfulness Precedes Empowerment
Elisha’s persistent following of Elijah illustrated faithfulness. Spiritual empowerment often follows steadfastness in our walk with God and service to others.
Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful. - 1 Corinthians 4:2 ASV
Dependence on the Holy Spirit
Just as Elisha depended on God’s Spirit, so must we. The real power for life and ministry comes not from ourselves, but from the indwelling Holy Spirit.
Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, saith Jehovah of hosts. - Zechariah 4:6 ASV
Passing the Baton of Faith
Elijah’s relationship with Elisha is a model of spiritual mentorship. We are called to invest in and raise up others for ministry, just as Paul did with Timothy.
And the things which thou hast heard from me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also. - 2 Timothy 2:2 ASV
Conclusion: Pursuing God’s Best for His Glory

Elisha’s request for a double portion invites us to seek God wholeheartedly, desiring to be filled with His Spirit for the work He has called us to do. It challenges us to pray boldly, serve faithfully, and depend entirely on God’s power—always for His glory and the advancement of His kingdom.
